solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female cut turkey

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches

explanation.surface: A hen bird has been butchered for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' looks like the bird being carved, but it is the slang sense of a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a show or film that fails badly, which is exactly a flop.

clue.text: Big canal boat bachelor put aside for learner

indicators.note: one letter is set aside and the other takes its place, so the swap is signalled here

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat used on canals
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A single man moves off a large narrowboat to make room for a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and big are plain synonyms describing something of great size.

clue.text: Politician's Dad you heard on series of items

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: heard tells us to take how the word sounds, giving a single letter

parts.note: the word you, said out loud
a list is a series of items written down

explanation.surface: A politician's father is overheard talking about a set of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Politician' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist is a politician who appeals directly to ordinary people against elites.

clue.text: Unexciting food, for example, Dorothy's briefly brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
Dot is the short form of Dorothy, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone mentions that Dorothy has served up some dull food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses EG + DOTS, which suits a down answer; 'briefly' trims Dorothy to her nickname Dot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling and bland food such as suet puddings, hence unexciting.

clue.text: Truly reflect Michigan trio of Republicans holding office at outset

parts.note: MI is the US postal abbreviation for Michigan

indicators.note: holding means the three letters close round what follows

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican, three times

indicators.note: at outset tells us to take only the opening letter of office

explanation.surface: Three Michigan Republicans in office faithfully represent their state's views from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the O from 'office at outset' inside RRR after the first R pair, giving RROR.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror something is to reproduce it faithfully, as a looking-glass gives an exact reflection.

clue.text: Method of travel on rise? Don't believe him!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on rise means the word goes upwards, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: rail is a means of transport, travelling by train

explanation.surface: A traveller boasts of a rising transport system, and the listener scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rise' turns RAIL upwards, a reversal suited to a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who should not be believed is one who tells untruths, a teller of falsehoods.

clue.text: Getting Old Boy practice after resistance dropped

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for Old Boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: dropped means the letter for resistance is removed from the word

parts.note: training is practice for a skill or sport
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A former pupil gets back into practice now that opposition has fallen away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes the R out of TRAINING to leave TAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining and getting are synonyms meaning acquiring or coming to have something.

clue.text: Some yoga — the recruits assemble

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: New recruits come together for a yoga session.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to come together in one place, the same as to assemble.

clue.text: In favour of quiet support

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone backs a cause without making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something placed underneath to hold a thing up, a physical support.

clue.text: Guarantee less than accurate reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means we want a word sounding like the phrase, not spelt like it

parts.note: jokingly, something less than right is under right

explanation.surface: A guarantee is said to be not entirely reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than accurate' is read as 'under right', and 'reportedly' gives a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To underwrite is to accept financial liability for something, in effect guaranteeing it.

clue.text: Friend hiding European ring

indicators.note: hiding means the friend wraps around and conceals the other letter

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend is concealing a ring belonging to a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery, but here it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a loud ringing of bells, so a ring in the sense of a sounding.

clue.text: Opening remark in ship on Arctic?

definitions.meaning: an ... is a comment made to ease tension when people first meet
an ... is a ship built to clear a way through frozen seas

explanation.surface: A captain makes a remark on starting a voyage through polar waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses involve breaking ice: social awkwardness, or the literal frozen sea in polar regions.

clue.text: Vehicle characterized by activity, last to go

indicators.note: last to go says the final letter of that word is removed

parts.note: busy means full of activity

explanation.surface: A vehicle known for being lively loses its final run.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers on a set route.

clue.text: Troublemaker's air got at cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troublemaker's tune is being taken apart by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Troublemaker' stands for 'is', a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up public unrest, a person who deliberately causes trouble.

clue.text: Big number, including other ranks, in swampy area

indicators.note: including says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a mass is a large quantity
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A large body of ordinary soldiers is bogged down in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or marshland, ground that is soft and wet.

clue.text: Education expert, most senior, flexible

indicators.note: flexible means able to bend into another shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The highest-ranking educationalist is said to be adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was an Italian educator who devised a child-centred teaching method.

clue.text: Bright in South — linger on

parts.note: to tarry is to linger or delay

explanation.surface: Someone bright in the south of the country stays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A starry sky is lit by many stars, so it is bright with points of light.

clue.text: Taciturn guy's unexpected story about East

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
unexpected means the word turns out in a surprising order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quiet man produces a surprising tale about the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' rearranges STORY to OYSTR, and 'about' wraps that round E. The 's after 'guy' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps quiet is said to be close as an oyster, a shellfish that clams shut.

clue.text: Ambush — hazard of course

definitions.meaning: an ambush is a ... set for an enemy
on a golf course a ... is a sand bunker, one of the hazards

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a snare: a surprise attack, or a sand-filled hollow on a golf course.

clue.text: Concur — a craving must be curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means docked at the tail, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: greed is an excessive craving

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees a desire has to be reined in.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to share the same opinion, which is what concurring means.

clue.text: Rearrange a space as in inland lake

indicators.note: rearrange is a direct instruction to put the following letters in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy a room as one would in a holiday spot by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian Sea is a landlocked body of water, the largest lake in the world.

clue.text: Paid poet on regular basis for musical instrument

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A poet is paid regularly to play an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple wind instrument, a tube blown into to make notes.

clue.text: Feature of car used in hasty retreat

indicators.note: used in means the answer is found sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A getaway car needs a particular feature for a quick escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the rubber covering on each wheel, part of every car.

clue.text: Fancy horse, Peru, one to bet on in crisis?

definitions.text: one to bet on in crisis?

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipster rates a fancied racehorse from Peru as a sure bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' and 'bet' suggest racing, and a favourite is a 'fancy', but the answer is the rescuer one relies on in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero is the comic-book saviour people rely on when disaster strikes.

clue.text: At first really envious, eying fine part of sail

indicators.note: at first says to take the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A sailor gazes enviously at a fine piece of canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a section of a sail that can be rolled or tied in to reduce its area in strong wind.
